Saddiq Bey 19 pointsMarch 21, 20268:32 PM CDTKarlo Matkovic soared for a highlight-reel, 360 alley oop dunk Saturday, putting New Orleans in front 95-81 early in the fourth quarter. Unfortunately for the Pelicans, their offense almost entirely vanished from there. Cleveland used a 13-0 run to draw within a point of its hosts, then dominated the final few minutes to take a 106-99 lead at 1:57. Donovan Mitchell sealed the outcome with an and-one layup at 4 seconds. The Cavaliers denied the Pelicans in their attempt to post an eighth straight home victory, which would’ve been their longest Smoothie King Center winning streak since 2008.After a quiet first half that was hampered by foul trouble, Zion Williamson erupted for a total of 25 points. Saddiq Bey added 19 points, but the club’s other starters experienced rough shooting nights. The Pelicans shot just 43 percent from the field and were 12/40 on three-point attempts (30 percent). Rotating back to a reserve role with Dejounte Murray in uniform, Yves Missi was a force in the paint, grabbing 10 rebounds and blocking three shots, including early rejections of Cleveland stars Mitchell (27 points) and Evan Mobley (18 points, eight rebounds).Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:00Remaining Time 0:00Zion Williamson Highlights vs. Cleveland Cavaliers 3/21/26BY THE NUMBERS60-42: Pelicans scoring edge in the middle quarters, with James Borrego calling them two of the team’s best defensive periods of the season. New Orleans went up 88-76 entering the final 12 minutes.55-40: Cleveland rebounding advantage. Borrego described Cavaliers offensive boards (14) as particularly costly in what turned into a clutch game, tight in the final five minutes. Several of those second chances occurred on critical NOLA defensive possessions.10-6: New Orleans record since the All-Star break, despite Saturday’s defeat. The Pelicans had not lost at home since Feb. 20 vs. Milwaukee, the first game coming out of the league's midseason hiatus.Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:00Remaining Time 0:00James Borrego | Pelicans-Cavaliers Postgame Interview 3/21/26NEXT FOR NEW ORLEANSAt this stage, the most compelling Pelicans games occur when they face opponents who have something at stake, as the regular season heads to an April 12 conclusion. That will be the case for their entire three-game road trip next week to New York, Detroit and Toronto.NEXT VS. CAVALIERSSaturday’s meeting concluded the season series. Unlike many previous campaigns, the Pelicans have compiled a fairly similar success rate against the East (9-17) as their own conference (16-30). Of course, some of that can be attributed to a West-heavy slate since the All-Star break, when New Orleans has played its best basketball. Normally the Pelicans have a markedly better interconference record than intraconference, because the West has been the superior half of the NBA for the majority of the franchise’s 22 seasons in the West.Photos: Pelicans vs. Cavaliers | Game Action 3/21/261 / 39NEW ORLEANS, LA - MARCH 21: Zion Williamson #1 of the New Orleans Pelicans drives to the basket during the game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on March 21, 2026 at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans, Louisiana.
